features.headline: Inside LeBron's first game in Philly — more than two decades ago
features.desc: Nearly 25 years ago, LeBron won over Philly for the first time — inside one of the most iconic basketball arenas in the world.
body: Jeremy Treatman, a former high school assistant coach in the Philadelphia suburbs who was running a burgeoning company that staged big-time basketball events between the game's future stars, had just sent a message to Dru Joyce II, the new coach at St. Vincent-St. Mary High School in Akron, Ohio, the school famously led by one of the most highly touted prep prospects in the history of the sport.

Six months after a then-17-year-old LeBron James had appeared on the cover of Sports Illustrated accompanied by the headline, "The Chosen One," Treatman was pitching Joyce on choosing him to build James' hype even more.

How would you like to play at the Palestra in Philly? How would you like to play Madison Square Garden against Sebastian Telfair? How would you like to play at Ohio State? How would you like to play at University of Dayton? How would you like to play in the Dean Dome in North Carolina?
In Philly parlance, Treatman had him at, "Yo."

"He calls me the next day and he says, 'You can get us to play at the Palestra?!'" Treatman told ESPN. "I go, 'Absolutely! Of course.' He goes, 'I've always dreamed of playing in the Palestra. I've heard about this place my whole life.
"I was completely bluffing about the Palestra," Treatman said. "I hadn't talked to anybody."

NAMED BY UNIVERSITY of Pennsylvania professor William N. Bates, evoking the Greek term "palæstra" that describes an athletic competition surrounded by an audience, the Palestra was the home for Penn's basketball, volleyball and wrestling teams.

features.headline: Knicks defend Taylor Swift's fandom after Tyler Kolek, Miles McBride weigh in
features.desc: Swift's history at Madison Square Garden includes courtside appearances dating back to 2014 and her July wedding to Travis Kelce.
body: Taylor Swift's New York Knicks fandom is up for debate — and the team itself has already weighed in. In an NBA 2K League video shared Thursday, Knicks guards Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride were asked to name the "fakest"

celebrity fan they'd seen courtside at an NBA game. Kolek floated Swift's name, and McBride agreed. "Maybe Taylor Swift? I don't know if I've seen her at any other games," Kolek said of the pop star's appearance at Game 4 of the NBA Finals.
Kolek acknowledged that Swift's schedule might keep her from getting to Madison Square Garden regularly, but he still referred to her fandom as "a little performative."

McBride pointed to two familiar faces at the Garden — Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan — as examples of "solid" celebrity fans. The Knicks, meanwhile, had a different read on Swift's courtside credentials.

"Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization," the team said in a statement to TMZ.
Swift has been photographed at Knicks games as far back as 2014, seven years before McBride joined the team and a decade before Kolek did.
She was last seen courtside at MSG on June 10, when the Knicks completed the largest comeback in NBA Finals history, overcoming a 29-point deficit in a 107-106 victory over the San Antonio Spurs.

Less than a month later, she returned to the Garden for her star-studded wedding to Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce on July 3. As for how Swift's fans might take the clip, Kolek had an idea. "I'm going to get some hate from the Swifties,"

features.headline: 3 ways Browns QB Shedeur Sanders can show growth vs. Saints
features.desc: The opportunity is a big one as the second-year quarterback's first start of the season comes at a critical time.
body: Before Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken announced on Aug. 24 that he was naming Deshaun Watson the team's starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders, he spoke with Sanders in his office about his forward-looking approach.
Ten weeks later, Sanders is poised to make his first start of the 2026 NFL season Sunday at the New Orleans Saints (1 p.m. ET, CBS) as Watson remains sidelined in the NFL's concussion protocol.
"He's very diligent and he likes to play football, has a natural confidence about him," Monken said Friday. "Just like any young player, they've got to play....
Where he's improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections.
There were so many things he needed to work on, and he's done that like any young player. Any young player has a lot to work on, especially at the quarterback position.
"And you can see that from the moment we got here and that's why we opened up the competition and we split the reps was because of his ascent."
Sanders' first start of the season comes at a critical time. The Browns are 5-3 after a Week 8 road loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers that knocked Cleveland out of first place in the AFC North.
ESPN Analytics gives the Browns a 16.5% chance of making the playoffs. A win against the Saints would increase their odds to 25.4% ahead of four straight home games.

Sanders made seven starts as a rookie last season and went 3-4 in those games, but he posted a 19.0 Total QBR, the fifth-lowest mark among 696 quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts in a season in the QBR era (since 2006).

features.headline: Joe Burrow makes time for art in Madrid ahead of Bengals-Falcons
features.desc: While in Spain, the Bengals quarterback is finding time for one of his off-field interests: art.
body: MADRID — Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow knows what he wants to do with his free time exploring Madrid ahead of Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. Forget football — well, at least the American kind.

The Cincinnati star, who attracted a massive media gathering Friday, said that if he gets a chance to wind down, he'd like to indulge one of his many off-field interests and see the art around the Spanish capital.
"I'd like to go see some more museums and go to an art gallery and do a little shopping, but we'll see," Burrow said.

The Pro Bowler and two-time MVP finalist already accomplished some of that earlier in the week when he stopped by the Museo del Prado during Cincinnati's first off day in Madrid. The team arrived from Cincinnati on Wednesday morning, which allowed him some time to go explore.

And even if he wasn't back home, it doesn't mean he didn't go unnoticed. He said he ran into a group of students from the United States who are studying abroad who recognized him. It's fitting for a person whose profile has grown well beyond the game in recent years.

"It's often a little more than I expect when I'm in a different country," Burrow said. "I usually expect to go pretty incognito and not have anybody recognize me. It's usually a little more than that. But I love being out here because I can feel like a normal person for a little bit."

Burrow and the Bengals (5-2) have spent the week trying to balance being tourists and also preparing for a showdown against the Falcons (3-5) at the historic Santiago Bernabeu stadium, which is home to Real Madrid.

features.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Jacoby Brissett, Jeffery Simmons, more
features.desc: Wise move for the Ravens to add Jacoby Brissett? Did the Bears give up too much to go all-in with Jeffery Simmons? Let's evaluate eight trades before the deadline.
body: NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, which is Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET.
When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks.

How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade.
Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here are our evaluations for eight deals of trading season, including two quarterback moves (Jacoby Brissett and J.J. McCarthy) and the massive blockbuster sending Jeffery Simmons to Chicago. Check back through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.
Jump to a trade: Brissett | Simmons | Buckner | Nelson Harrison | Jurgens | Porter | McCarthy
Ravens get: QB Jacoby Brissett, 2027 fifth-round pick Cardinals get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 seventh-round pick

With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both hurt, the Ravens are throwing a Hail Mary to save their season. Baltimore is trading for veteran Brissett, shortly after the Cardinals benched him in favor of Gardner Minshew II.
Brissett is a respected bridge quarterback and has played around expectations this season in Arizona. He has a 48.9 QBR, which ranks 23rd out of 30 qualifying starters.

That number alone is probably selling Brissett's performance short this season, though, considering he was playing behind the O-line unit that ranked 31st in pass block win rate and was able to use play-action just 18% of the time (27th most).

features.headline: LeBron James vs. Cleveland: Top performances against Cavaliers
features.desc: James holds a 9-4 record with averages of 29.6 points, 8.5 rebounds and 6.9 assists per game on 54% shooting in Cleveland as an opponent.
body: LeBron James returns to familiar territory on Friday as the Philadelphia 76ers face the Cleveland Cavaliers on the road in an NBA Cup game.

A native of Akron, Ohio, James attended St. Vincent-St. Mary High School in the city, becoming one of the nation's most highly touted prospects. The Cavaliers selected James with the No. 1 pick in the 2003 NBA draft.

James, who spent 11 seasons with the Cavaliers across two separate stints with the team, often shifts into an extra gear when he returns home. Holding a 9-4 record, he's averaging 29.6 points, 8.5 rebounds and 6.9 assists per game on 54% shooting in Cleveland as an opponent.
In November 2023, James described returning to play at home as "just special."

"Stepping back on this floor is always a pretty cool feeling, looking up there and pretty much being a part of all of the banners in this arena," James said. "And the No. 1 banner, the one that sits in the middle, was that '16 championship, so that's pretty cool."
Here's a look back at James' notable games against the Cavaliers in Cleveland.
Stats: 38 points, 12 assists, 10 rebounds, 58.6% shooting
In the middle of a down season in Los Angeles, James dominated during his trip back home.

He scored 17 points in the second quarter en route to a 38-point triple-double, becoming the sixth player in NBA history with at least three triple-doubles against his former team, according to the Elias Sports Bureau.

It also marked his third triple-double against the Cavaliers, all of which have come on the road. The only other players in NBA history with three triple-doubles against their former team in their building are Domantas Sabonis and Fat Lever.
